title: Note on a Cemetery at Karm al-Shaikh, Jerusalem
author: (unsigned in the text read)
location_note: Karm al-Shaikh, about 40 m north of the north-east corner of the Old City wall (site of the Palestine Archaeological Museum), Jerusalem; placed by name. Pages 3-5 confirmed by QDAP III p. 48 ('Vol. I, pp. 3-5').
reading: full (pp. 3-5); the following rotated leaves (coin summary table and plates) not read: OCR unusable
notes: Clearance during the Museum foundation works: 68 rock-cut cist graves (slab-covered, re-used), 5 caves (A-D intercommunicating; B with 26 skulls), 4 rock-cut chambers with rock-sunk graves and roof openings (E, G, H, J; coin of Arcadius in G), one sarcophagus with gold ear-rings, two tombstones. Coins from the end of the 2nd c. BC to the 6th c. AD and later give the site's span only; no tomb is dated individually.
